answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored reputation: each agent locks a refundable deposit behind one persistent identity anchor, such as a public key with a verifiable history of completed work. New identities start at zero trust and earn it only through costly, checkable service, so an attacker spinning up thousands of Sybils pays a linear cost per identity and cannot simply echo the same reputation across all of them. Cheat, and the deposit is slashed and the anchor burned, a permanent umber mark on the ledger that no fresh alias can wash away.
